segments.speaker: Participant
segments.segment_type: initial risk assessment and access decision
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Around 06:40 ... my first thought went straight to the rockburst at our sister operation two months back ... I treated the report as more likely to be heading toward something serious ... I went with enhanced monitoring and limited access.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Initial risk is explicitly linked to recall of the vivid recent sister-mine rockburst despite no current alarm.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The 05:00 baseline was 0.2mm ... By 09:40 it had moved to 0.6mm ... compared to this morning, it's still a small number ... I didn't go back to the GCMP's rate-of-change table.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explains the comparison rule used for the updated extensometer reading and acknowledges that the rate criterion was not applied.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.segment_type: supervisor credibility weighting and access decision
segments.raw_interview_anchor: He mentioned hearing similar popping back in 2009 ... His track record carried a lot of weight for me in that moment.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Supervisor tenure and reassurance receive substantial weight without checking whether the historical comparison fits current conditions.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.segment_type: crack comparison and visual evidence interpretation
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Today's crack looked about the same width to me ... I read it as consistent with what we already knew was fine ... I was judging the crack against the old photo instead of against the newer number.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The prior crack photograph is used as the reference while the new seismic threshold is not integrated.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Putting it together ... it read as a pretty clean explanation: cooling stress plus the handover timing plus residual vibration from that blast.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Several plausible factors are presented as one clean causal explanation despite no factor being confirmed as dominant.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I focused mainly on the miner who first reported the sounds ... I did mention the missing engineer sign-off ... but it came across more as a process note than a central cause.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Responsibility is centered on the individual miner while the missing GCMP engineer sign-off is secondary.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Less than when I wrote it. It felt like a complete picture at the time, but there were threads I didn't fully chase down.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a confidence judgment but does not express another hidden bias mechanism.

main_failure_modes: The supervisor-tenure finding is correctly localized and mechanistically complete but uses the near-neighbor authority-bias label instead of Experience Bias.
The crack-photo finding uses the near-neighbor confirmation-bias label and only partially captures the distinct photographic-reference anchoring mechanism.
The Attribution Bias finding is low confidence, so it is absent from the recommended high_and_moderate threshold.
main_strengths: All six findings are correctly localized with valid supporting quotations.
Availability, instrument-baseline anchoring, narrative fallacy, and attribution are captured with full mechanisms and exact or approved labels.
The RAG discloses that corpus support was unavailable and states plausible non-bias interpretations.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The run shows strong segment detection and generally faithful evidence use, with a measurable ontology gap between strict label matching and mechanism-first matching. The relaxed production deadline does not undermine the six evidence-processing findings; the main losses arise from two taxonomy/mechanism decisions and one conservative confidence tier.
